Chinese foundation models have consolidated around a small number of major technology platforms, with ByteDance, Baidu, Tencent, and Alibaba each operating their own large language models alongside smaller competitors.

This concentration reflects the capital and compute requirements that gate entry to foundation model development. Building and operating these systems demands sustained infrastructure investment that only established technology companies with existing data center footprints can absorb. The list does not reveal the underlying compute capacity, power consumption, or physical infrastructure behind each model, so it cannot directly measure the building and power constraints that shape this market.

The uniform data governance note across all seven models signals a structural difference in how Chinese foundation models operate relative to their counterparts elsewhere. Users crossing borders with data face uniform regulatory surface. The data does not explain whether this reflects technical architecture, legal requirements, or operational policy, nor does it cover adoption rates, model size, or performance characteristics that would indicate which systems command the most compute resources.
